parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the clean-room benchmark constraint, the need to reproduce codesnap-cli behavior, and the broad CLI/rendering surface including output formats, config, text/image inputs, ranges, line numbers, breadcrumbs, warnings, and clipboard errors.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split early fact-finding to doc_probe and cli_probe, later started semantics_probe, attempted one more render child that hit the thread limit, and kept implementation ownership with the parent rather than delegating a finished component.
parallel.implementation: After interrupting the active probes, the parent tried a Rust implementation with external crates, encountered dependency resolution failure, checked available libraries, and pivoted to a Python/Pillow/Pygments-style standalone implementation with compile.sh installing codesnap.py as executable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent alone assembled the final deliverable after the child probe interruption; no completed child implementation was merged, and no file collision or artifact leakage was visible.
parallel.verification: The parent performed smoke checks for version, simple rendering, silent mode, ASCII warning, clipboard failure, and final PNG generation, but did not show the deeper post-pivot geometry and uncommon flag checks that the serial trajectory performed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final answer itself notes residual risk in less common flags after the dependency-free Python pivot, and the current official evaluation failed with 183 of 516 evaluated cases passed.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room task and systematically derived the CLI help surface, error behavior, text/image input modes, range handling, execution mode, rendering options, and geometry expectations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, and verification continuously, so observations stayed in one working context without child handoff or join boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial run first attempted a Rust CLI, hit the same dependency limitation, then pivoted to a Python implementation and iteratively refined input handling, output formats, rendering, fonts, line splitting, and geometry.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact was assembled through compile.sh and codesnap.py in the same workspace by the same owner; no delegation merge or shared-state coordination issue was present.
serial.verification: The serial run verified help/version/no-argument behavior, image stdin, output dimensions, large README rendering performance, line numbers, breadcrumbs, and range geometry after implementation changes.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process timed out before a final assistant response, and the official evaluation still failed, but the produced artifact passed 449 of 516 evaluated cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering constraints and broad codesnap CLI/rendering obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and derived a fuller behavior map from direct CLI and rendering probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The task requirements were identical, but serial carried more observed edge behavior into implementation and validation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split exploration into doc, CLI, and semantics probes while the parent remained the implementer and final assembler.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and kept all ownership in one continuous trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child lifecycle dependencies without completed child handoffs; serial avoided that boundary by keeping observations and edits local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs are redacted, no completed child result was available, and the parent did not receive a stable handoff from active probe children before proceeding.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept discovered requirements, fixes, and measurements in the same agent context throughout the run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The meaningful context difference was not a proven missing brief or bad contract; it was the loss of pending probe context through early interruption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel attempted Rust, hit dependency/network limits, pivoted to Python, and delivered a single Python executable wrapper through compile.sh.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial followed the same broad Rust-to-Python pivot but spent more iterations on behavior and rendering details before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both settled on Python after Rust dependencies were unavailable; serial applied more targeted post-pivot fixes and geometry tuning.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children were running after waits and then explicitly interrupted, with child logs recording aborted turns instead of completed results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all observations and edits remained in the one active agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The core coordination difference is that parallel stopped active probe children before their results finalized, while serial had no join boundary to lose.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final assembly was parent-local after child interruption; there is no evidence of concurrent file collision or consumed child artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced codesnap.py and compile.sh through one owner and continued refining that same deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The runs differ in child lifecycle rather than shared workspace corruption; neither shows a retained shared-state pattern.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed smoke tests and reported version/rendering checks, but final text admits less common flags were not exhaustively rechecked.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial repeatedly checked CLI behavior, image input, compile status, performance, and exact output dimensions for multiple options.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was broader and better tied to renderer geometry, while parallel verification was narrower after the child probe cutoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent time waiting on children, then cut them off and closed with known residual unverified areas.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial eventually timed out before a final assistant response, but the generated artifact was evaluated and had much higher coverage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget pressure manifested as interrupted active child probes; serial pressure manifested as missing final response, not a delegation error.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations make this a both_fail pair: parallel passed 183 of 516 evaluated cases and serial passed 449 of 516. The official outcome is therefore not discordant, but the serial artifact was materially stronger. The clearest evidenced process difference is that parallel spawned useful probe children, then interrupted them while they were still active and before a completed handoff, whereas serial kept the same observations and fixes in one continuous loop and performed more rendering and geometry verification.
parallel_contributors: Parallel interrupted active doc, CLI, and semantics probes before any completed child result was consumed.
Parallel then implemented and verified locally from a narrower evidence base, with final residual risk in less common flags.
serial_contributors: Serial preserved a continuous probe-to-implementation context with no child join boundary.
Serial performed later post-pivot geometry, image-input, range, line-number, and breadcrumb checks.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts still had implementation defects against hidden official tests; the serial defect set was smaller by evaluated pass count.
The dependency failure and Python pivot were ordinary environment/implementation events shared by both attempts, not themselves concurrency labels.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process contributor to lower coverage, not an official pass/fail outcome difference or exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly owned implementation after the probes and produced the final executable, so implementation was not ownerless.
No multiple completed component implementations required an unowned reconciliation step; the parent assembled the final artifact locally.
The parent created the final Python executable path and compile script, so final assembly had an owner.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from implementation to smoke verification and delivery after reclaiming the child slots.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; the parent probed and later implemented while child probes were still part of the plan.
The parallel investigation did overlap across children, but it was not completed as a separate first phase; the direct failure was interrupting active probes before results finalized.
The indispensable implementation path stayed with the parent and was not starved by auxiliary workers; the directly evidenced episode is child cancellation.
Several probes were active, but there is no separate collective fan-out exhaustion episode beyond the same interruption chain.
The child tasks were probe scopes, the briefs are redacted, and no single demonstrably overbroad child assignment is needed to explain the observed consequence.
The child brief payloads are encrypted/redacted, and the logs do not prove that a known requirement was omitted from a child's initial delegation.
The delegated work was probing rather than separately owned interoperating components, and no incompatible produced components or contracts are visible.
No specific known finding is visible before transfer and then absent after transfer; the key child information never finalized into a handoff.
No returned child report was too large or poorly structured for the parent to reduce; no completed handoff was returned at all.
The parent did not consume a superseded child report or stale workspace state before acting.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
The parent performed end-to-end smoke checks before final response; hidden evaluator failure and admitted residual risk are not sufficient for this label.
There was no replacement or retry agent visibly repeating prior work without inherited checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent observed active probe children and explicitly interrupted them before their needed probe work or result finalized, then proceeded locally from a narrower evidence base.
candidates.realized_consequence: Active probe work was stopped before completed child results could be handed back or consumed, after which the parent delivered a narrower implementation with lower official coverage.
candidates.near_match_reason: No completed child result was available to the parent and ignored; the failure point is cancellation before result finalization.

candidates.reason: No complete, directly promotable child candidate or compatible component set existed and was merely finalized too late.
No child result or implementation change was merged after verification without a post-merge check.
The children were probe/research agents, not completed delegated implementation owners with retrievable code that the parent failed to join.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent; the relevant children were active probes interrupted before final return.
After cancellation the parent did take over by moving into local implementation and verification; the defect is the premature stop, not absence of takeover.
The parent did not ignore an available completed child result; the children were still running and then were interrupted.
The parent waited, listed active agents, and sent messages before interrupting; it was not merely waiting blindly until the deadline.
There are no independently produced overlapping implementation files or competing cross-file designs requiring reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file with a resulting reconciliation problem.
No non-entry source file produced or owned by one actor is shown being replaced by another actor.
The parent created the final deliverable after child interruption; no other live actor owned or replaced the submitted executable or entry-point source.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Shared workspace access alone is insufficient, and no concrete unstable-state or provenance consequence from concurrent writes is visible.
No generated child file, cache, temporary output, process, or auxiliary implementation was consumed by another actor as stable input.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parent spawned active probe children, observed them still running, then explicitly interrupted them before a completed result was finalized or consumed. Serial kept the analogous probing and refinement in one continuous context.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Active probe work was interrupted before completed child results could be handed back or consumed, leaving the parent to close from a narrower local probe and verification set.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: No completed child result was visible and ignored; the directly observed problem is stopping running children before result finalization.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, Blind Timeout Wait, No Failure Takeover, Missing Verifier Return, and Unused Completed Result were reviewed as same-chain or near-match candidates, but the direct boundary was early interruption of active probe children.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no additional independent ownership, context, join, monitoring, write, retry, or contamination episode cleared the retention gate.
